latest_release.body:
> 25 new sites, a dozen MangaHub mirrors that learned to decrypt their pages, and a few Cloudflare-guarded sites that download again.

## Highlights

Manga Downloader now supports **581 sites**, 25 more than 25.1.0.

### ✨ New sites

- **revivalscans.com** (English). Paid chapters are listed as locked and skipped, and chapter links load the whole series. (#463)
- **resetscans.net** (English) and **pornhwareader.com** (English, NSFW). (#461)
- **komikzona.my.id** (Indonesian), **merlinshoujo.com** (Turkish) and **w6.dandadan.net** (English, single series). (#457)
- 19 sites through grabbers we already had (#456):
  - English: desirescans.com, hirayareads.com, kensscan.com, mangabolt.com (use a series URL), mangagg.com, mangahub.us, mangakakalove.com, mangareadz.com, manhwaus.net
  - English, NSFW: allporncomic.com, lgbtics.com, readmanga18.com
  - Spanish: scan-inmortal.com; Spanish, NSFW: ikuhentai.net, spanish.seraphic-deviltry.com
  - Turkish: mangakulesi.com; Turkish, NSFW: nonafansub.com
  - Hebrew: mangashelf.co.il; Thai: up-manga.com

### 🐛 Fixes

- **MangaHub and its mirrors** (mangahub.io, mangahub.us, 1manga.co, mangakakalot.fun, manganel.me, mangafox.fun, mangatoday.fun, mangaonline.fun, mangareader.site, mangapanda.onl, mangahere.onl, onemanga.info) weren't recognised after the platform moved its API, and they now encrypt their page lists. Both are handled, so all twelve download again. (#464)
- **paradise-bl.com**, **gaiatoon.com** and **arcurafansub.com** now sit behind a Cloudflare check that only a visible browser window gets past, so they open one. (#464)
- **Sites read through a browser**: when Cloudflare's check handed over to the page mid-load, some series ended in "unsupported site". The page is read again once it settles. (#464)
- **templetoons.com** downloads again: its reader loads pages as you scroll, and its image server refused our requests. A reader that loads fewer pages than it has now fails instead of saving a short chapter. (#464)
- **manhuatop.org** moved to a new design and downloads again. (#461)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/elboletaire/manga-downloader/compare/v25.1.0...v25.2.0

[Website][website] • [Features](#features) • [Installation](#installation) • [Desktop app](#using-the-desktop-app---guide) • [Command line](#using-the-command-line---guide) • [Supported sites](#supported-sites) • [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
Manga Downloader downloads manga chapters from MangaDex and more than 500 other sites and packs them into CBZ, CBR or EPUB files, ready to read on your e-reader or in your favorite comic app. It comes as a **desktop app** for Windows, macOS and Linux, and as a **command line tool** for scripts, servers and Docker.
## Features - **[581 supported sites](#supported-sites)**, from big aggregators to small scanlation groups. - In the app, **paste a URL and it loads**: the series, its chapters and the languages and scanlation groups it offers appear on their own. - **Pick what you need**: chapter ranges such as `1,3,5-10` (Shift+click or *All* in the app), and the language or scanlation group you want, on sites that host several versions of a chapter. - **Keep a folder up to date**: `--skip-existing` leaves out the chapters you already have, so a scheduled run only fetches the new ones. - **E-reader friendly output**: AVIF pages are converted to JPEG, so they don't show up blank on Kobo, KOReader or Calibre (WebP too, if you ask). - **Flexible output**: one file per chapter, per volume or for everything, as CBZ, CBR, EPUB or plain image folders, named from a template. - **Skip pages** such as credits or ads (`--skip-pages`). - In the app, **live progress**: every chapter shows up as it's fetched and packed, with a summary and an *Open folder* button when it's done. - **Sites that need a browser** (JavaScript or Cloudflare) work too: the tool drives a Chromium-based browser you already have and clicks the "Verify you are human" box for you. - **Concurrent downloads** with retries. - **Command line**: a single binary with no runtime, no dependencies and no config file, plus Docker images. - **Desktop app**: native folder picker, and a window that follows your system's light or dark theme. ## Installation ### Installing the desktop app [![Desktop app downloads][app downloads badge]][releases] The easiest way is the [website][website], which picks the right download for your system. Or get it from the [releases page][releases]: - **Windows**: `manga-downloader-gui--windows-amd64-installer.exe`, or `-windows-arm64-installer.exe` for ARM devices such as Snapdragon laptops. It installs for your user alone (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Manga Downloader`), or for everyone (`C:\Program Files\Manga Downloader`) when run as administrator, and adds a Start menu shortcut. For a portable copy, use the `.zip` of the same name instead: unzip it and run `manga-downloader-gui.exe`. - **macOS**: `manga-downloader-gui--darwin-universal.zip`. Unzip it and move `Manga Downloader.app` wherever you like. Or install it with [Homebrew][homebrew], which also puts `manga-downloader-gui` on your `PATH`: ~~~bash brew install --cask elboletaire/tap/manga-downloader-app ~~~ If you installed the app under its old name, `manga-downloader`, run `brew uninstall --cask manga-downloader` first. - **Linux**: `manga-downloader-gui--linux-amd64.tar.gz`, or `-linux-arm64.tar.gz`. Extract it and run `install.sh` to add the app to your applications menu. It installs for your user only, into `~/.local`, with no root needed. Run it again to update, or with `--uninstall` to remove it (set the same `XDG_DATA_HOME`, if you used one): ~~~bash tar -xzf manga-downloader-gui--linux-amd64.tar.gz ./manga-downloader-gui--linux-amd64/install.sh ~~~ Or just run `manga-downloader-gui` from the extracted folder. It needs WebKitGTK 4.1 (`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` on Debian and Ubuntu), which most desktops already have; `install.sh` tells you how to get it if it's missing. > [!NOTE] > **macOS** doesn't sign the app, so Gatekeeper blocks its first launch: allow it > once under *System Settings → Privacy & Security* ([FAQ][faq-gatekeeper]). > > **Windows** may show SmartScreen's *"Windows protected your PC"* for the > installer or the app, for the same reason: click **More info** → **Run anyway** > ([FAQ][faq-smartscreen]). The app also needs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 > runtime, which Windows 11 and current Windows 10 already have; without it, the > app offers to install it on first launch. If the desktop app sits next to the command line tool or is on your `PATH` (the Homebrew cask and the Linux `install.sh` put it there), `manga-downloader ui` opens it. On Windows, double-clicking `manga-downloader.exe` does the same. The app checks for a newer release when it starts and offers to update itself. Settings (the gear icon, or Ctrl+, / ⌘,) turns that off and sets the app's language; the [app guide](docs/app.md#settings-and-the-update-check) says what the check sends. ### Installing the command line tool [![CLI downloads][cli downloads badge]][releases] #### Homebrew On macOS and Linux, install the command line tool from [Homebrew][homebrew]: ~~~bash brew install elboletaire/tap/manga-downloader ~~~ Homebrew doesn't quarantine the command line tool, so there's no Gatekeeper step on macOS. `brew upgrade manga-downloader` updates it. Completions for bash, zsh and fish are installed as well. That's the command line tool alone; the [desktop app](#installing-the-desktop-app) is the `manga-downloader-app` cask. Install both and `manga-downloader ui` opens the app: ~~~bash brew install elboletaire/tap/manga-downloader elboletaire/tap/manga-downloader-app ~~~ #### Prebuilt binary Builds are published for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, plus 32-bit builds for Linux and Windows (the latter named `windows-32bit-legacy`). Download the archive for your system from the [releases page][releases], extract it and run the binary: ~~~bash ./manga-downloader --help ~~~ To verify the download, check it against `manga-downloader--SHA256SUMS.txt` from the same release: `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing manga-downloader--SHA256SUMS.txt`. To run it from any folder, move the binary to a folder in your `PATH`, such as `/usr/local/bin` on Linux and macOS. `manga-downloader completion bash|zsh|fish|powershell` prints a shell completion script. For zsh, for example: ~~~bash manga-downloader completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_manga-downloader" ~~~ `manga-downloader completion --help` explains how to set up the other shells.
Windows: step-by-step setup
> [!IMPORTANT] > This is the command line tool, so run it from a terminal as shown below: > double-clicking `manga-downloader.exe` only shows the help ([FAQ][faq-exe]). 1. Open **PowerShell**: press the Start button, type `PowerShell` and press Enter. 2. Paste this line and press Enter: ~~~powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elboletaire/manga-downloader/master/install.ps1 | iex ~~~ 3. Close the terminal and open a new one. Then run it from any folder: ~~~cmd manga-downloader https://mangadex.org/title/a1c7c817-4e59-43b7-9365-09675a149a6f/one-piece 1-10 ~~~ The [install script](./install.ps1) downloads the latest release to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\manga-downloader` and adds that folder to your `PATH`. It doesn't need administrator rights. Run the same line again to update, and delete that folder to uninstall. > [!TIP] > Files are saved in the folder the terminal is in. To download straight into > a folder, open it in File Explorer, type `cmd` in the address bar and press > Enter. A terminal opens there, ready to use.
Prefer not to run a script?
Download the `windows-amd64` zip from the [releases page][releases] (or `windows-arm64` if you have an ARM device, such as a Snapdragon laptop), extract it, and copy `manga-downloader.exe` to `C:\Windows\System32`. Windows asks for administrator permission. After that, `manga-downloader` works in any terminal. > [!WARNING] > It works, but `System32` is Windows' own folder: it needs administrator > rights, and updating or uninstalling means replacing or deleting the file > there yourself. If SmartScreen shows *"Windows protected your PC"*, click **More info** → **Run anyway** ([why][faq-smartscreen]).
On macOS, Gatekeeper blocks the unsigned binary the first time: allow it once under *System Settings → Privacy & Security* ([FAQ][faq-gatekeeper]). #### Docker [![Docker Pulls][pulls badge]][docker hub] ~~~bash docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/downloads" elboletaire/manga-downloader [url] [chapters] ~~~ Files are written to the mounted `/downloads` folder, owned by user and group `1000`; if yours differ, add `-e USER_ID=$(id -u) -e GROUP_ID=$(id -g)`. The default image has no browser. For sites marked with `*`, use the `:browser` image, which ships Chromium and a virtual display: ~~~bash docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD:/downloads" elboletaire/manga-downloader:browser [url] [chapters] ~~~ `:latest` and `:browser` follow releases; `:master` and `:master-browser` are the development version.
Showing the browser window on your own display
The `:browser` image passes Cloudflare challenges on its own. If a challenge needs a real person, the browser window opens by itself, so forward your display to see it on your Linux desktop. You may need to run `xhost +local:` first: ~~~bash docker run --rm -it -e DISPLAY=$DISPLAY -v /tmp/.X11-unix:/tmp/.X11-unix \ -v "$PWD:/downloads" elboletaire/manga-downloader:browser [url] [chapters] ~~~
## Using the desktop app - [guide](docs/app.md) Not installed yet? Get it from the [website][website], or see [Installation](#installing-the-desktop-app). Paste a URL and it loads. Pick chapters with the range box, Shift+click or *All*, choose the language and scanlation group when the site offers them, set the folder, format and packing in *Options*, then press *Download*. The *Activity* tab shows progress, and the summary's *Open folder* button takes you to the files. Files go to your Downloads folder unless you choose another, and your options are remembered for next time. The [desktop app guide](docs/app.md) walks through every step and option, with screenshots. ## Using the command line - [guide](docs/cli.md) Not installed yet? See [Installation](#installing-the-command-line-tool). ~~~bash manga-downloader [flags] [url] [chapters] ~~~ - `url` is the manga's **index page**, the page that lists all its chapters. The URL of a single chapter works too: it resolves to the whole series. - `chapters` is a list of numbers and ranges, such as `1,3,5-10`, or `all`. Leave it out and the tool asks before downloading the whole series. Arguments aren't positional, so `manga-downloader 1-50 [url]` works too. `manga-downloader list [url]` prints the chapters, languages, groups and volumes without downloading, as JSON with `--json`; the app has no counterpart, as its chapter panel shows the same ([guide](docs/cli.md#listing-a-series)). A few of its flags: ~~~bash # one language, where the site lists several manga-downloader --language es [url] 1-10 # one file per volume, as the site files them manga-downloader --volumes auto [url] 1-20 # everything in a single file manga-downloader --bundle [url] 1-8 # EPUB instead of CBZ manga-downloader --format epub [url] 1-8 # only the chapters not in the folder yet, no questions asked manga-downloader --skip-existing -o ~/Manga/Series [url] all ~~~ `manga-downloader help` lists every flag; the [command line guide](docs/cli.md) explains them: languages and scanlation groups, bundles and volumes, image conversion, skipping pages, skipping existing files, file name templates and environment variables. ## Supported sites

If one doesn't, [open an issue][issues] or send a pull request. ## Troubleshooting The [FAQ on the website][faq] has the answers (also in Spanish, Catalan and Japanese): - [Windows says "Windows protected your PC"][faq-smartscreen] - [macOS won't open it][faq-gatekeeper] - [Double-clicking `manga-downloader.exe` just flashes a window][faq-exe] - [The newest chapter downloads empty or is missing][faq-paywall] - [Old chapters are missing, or a warning says the range starts before the first chapter][faq-old] - [A browser window pops up][faq-browser] - [No browser found][faq-nobrowser] - [Pages don't show up on my e-reader][faq-ereader] - [My site isn't supported][faq-unsupported] ## Building from source The command line tool needs Go 1.26 or newer (`go.mod`): ~~~bash make install # download dependencies make build # test and build ./manga-downloader ~~~ The desktop app is a [Wails](https://wails.io) app: a Go program showing a React frontend in the system's webview. It needs Go 1.26 or newer (`gui/go.mod`), Node 22, pnpm 12, and on Linux the WebKitGTK 4.1 and GTK 3 development headers (`libgtk-3-dev libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu): ~~~bash make build/gui # build ./manga-downloader-gui (frontend first) make build/gui/linux # the release's wails build into gui/build/bin/ (also /windows, /darwin) make test/gui # the GUI's vet, race tests and frontend tests make install/wails # the wails CLI the release builds with ~~~ ## A note on AI AI tools have changed what this project can be. For years, manga-downloader gained maybe one site a year. With AI, it grew a desktop app and went from 10 supported sites to over 500 in a matter of days. It isn't "vibe coded", though. Its foundations, the way sites are plugged in and how chapters are fetched and packed, are the ones I wrote by hand long before AI was involved, and the architecture is still my call. I review every change before it lands. Each change also has to pass the tests, and a site has to pass a real download checked with `verify-cbz`. Contributions go through the same review: pull requests are judged on design, correctness and evidence, whoever or whatever wrote them. Responsible use of AI is welcome. The repository ships an `AGENTS.md` and skills for coding agents, so an agent working on it starts from the project's conventions. ## Star history
